comparator.name: Artificial Intelligence
comparator.academicYear: 2026–2027; adopted TER and year-specific official course pages checked 26 October 2026
comparator.route: General Artificial Intelligence pathway without an optional specialisation
comparator.sourceNotes: For the general 2026–27 pathway, the TER lists 54 EC of compulsory first-year units plus one 6-EC restricted choice (first-listed Information Management); 42 EC of compulsory second-year units plus three 6-EC restricted choices (first-listed Robot Interaction, Data Structures and Algorithms for AI, AI in Health); and 24 EC compulsory third-year project, ethics and research-design units plus one 6-EC restricted choice (first-listed Cognitive Psychology for AI) and 30 EC genuinely open academic minor/profiling space. The zero-credit language test is excluded. This broad coherent 180-EC route has no optional specialisation credential. The TER permits incoming 2026–27 students to opt into Intelligent Systems or Socially Aware Computing under transitional rules, which are not required for this generic target. Every selected restricted choice is one valid unit; other listed options are not combined or presented as mandatory. Independent re-audit confirms the credit allocation. Bachelor project entry requires passed 6 EC introductory Python and at least 90 EC of AI bachelor curricular courses. Research Design requires four in-person working groups alongside the project. Diagnostic English test and required refresher are mandatory without extra credit. Ordinary BSA42 EC applies, subject to exceptions. The 2026–27 specialisation transition requires programme coordinator/board contact and24EC specialist choices plus6EC Project Socially Aware Computing; no specialisation credential is claimed here.

alternatives.label: Hybrid intelligence and human cognition
alternatives.concept: Combines programming, machine learning, logic and agent decision making with cognitive science, perception and human behaviour. Ethics and philosophy of mind frame how intelligent systems interact with people; this is a broad AI programme rather than a replica of the VU thesis and project sequence. General or biological courses supply their stated foundations; no specialised human–robot interaction, clinical AI, computational language project or independent AI thesis is guaranteed.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum includes extensive technical AI as well as cognition, interaction and ethics; hybrid intelligence describes the actual combination.
progression: Programming and calculus precede intermediate computation. Linear algebra precedes machine learning; probability/statistics is earlier in the cognition and health paths and concurrent with machine learning in the systems path. Both precede final neural-network and reinforcement-learning work. Machine Learning has no formal workbook prerequisite; concurrent probability is advisory preparation, not an invented pass requirement. Actual workbook prerequisites and offerings are checked for every placement. Psychology and neuroscience build from brain/behaviour and introductory neurobiology. Algorithms and advanced algorithms use the preceding programming and algorithm sequence; broad logic is complementary rather than an invented prerequisite.

alternatives.label: AI algorithms and computer systems
alternatives.concept: Emphasises intelligent agents, machine learning and neural networks alongside software development, algorithms, databases, numerical methods and computing infrastructure. Human interaction and ethics remain foundations, but the additional curriculum develops technical computer-science depth. General or biological courses supply their stated foundations; no specialised human–robot interaction, clinical AI, computational language project or independent AI thesis is guaranteed.
alternatives.labelReason: The 24 courses devote considerably more space to technical computer science and mathematics than the other programmes.
alternatives.distinctness: Five courses replace cognitive science and social psychology with networks, software engineering, advanced algorithms and numerical/multivariable mathematical methods; this is a materially different route into AI system construction.

routeSelection.route: General Artificial Intelligence pathway without an optional specialisation
routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic bachelor. The adopted 2026–27 TER makes Intelligent Systems and Socially Aware Computing optional, with transitional conditions for entrants; the ordinary curriculum with first-listed permitted constrained choices is a broad valid 180-EC path. No specialisation is chosen for a stronger UCR match.

selection.assessment: Three conceptually distinct, evidenced UCR curricula pass the 24-course and pairwise 30-EC distinctness gates: broad hybrid intelligence and cognition, technical AI system construction, and health/behaviour applications. The energy-systems interest is a separate application direction but the approved maximum of three alternatives is already reached; the isolated teaching direction lacks a specific UCR teacher-education sequence. Re-audit retains three qualified responses only because each has a substantial actual AI-method backbone and a distinct subject emphasis. Domain health/behaviour courses are not claimed to implement specialist medical AI. Sustainable-energy AI remains an unselected direction at the maximum of three, not a claim that generic AI courses alone provide energy engineering.

notes.text: VU requires dedicated intelligent-systems and socially-aware projects, human–computer and robot interaction, text mining, AI research design and an individual 15 EC bachelor project. UCR supplies substantial AI, computation and domain foundations with important gaps. General psychology is not computational human-behaviour modelling, and robotic motion planning is not a social-robot design course.

The VU individual AI project includes literature, research, a thesis and a poster presentation. UCR course projects do not automatically provide that supervised independent project. Optional independent research is additional to the displayed 180 EC and requires separate approval.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Artificial Intelligence combines computing and mathematics with human cognition and responsible AI. Its general bachelor includes programming, intelligent systems, machine learning, knowledge and data, computational human behaviour and social applications, alongside restricted choices, open academic study space and an individual AI research project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers three qualified directions: hybrid intelligence and cognition; AI algorithms and computer systems; and AI methods with health and behaviour foundations. Each contains substantial actual AI methods. Mathematics supports the computational sequence, while psychology, neuroscience and health courses supply domain knowledge. These compositions leave gaps in dedicated interaction design, computational behaviour modelling, text mining and the VU project sequence. They do not promise clinical AI validation, social-robot construction or an equivalent independent thesis.

curriculum.routeLabel: General AI pathway; no optional specialisation
curriculum.limitation: The general route comprises54EC compulsory year-one courses plus one6EC restricted choice;42EC compulsory year-two courses plus three6EC restricted choices;24EC prescribed year-three project/ethics/research-design plus one6EC restricted choice and30EC open academic profiling. First-listed eligible choices are shown; options and optional specialisations are not stacked. Project entry requires passed introductory Python6EC and at least90EC of AI bachelor curricular courses. The individual project requires a supervisor/topic, literature study, thesis and annual seminar poster presentation; assessment is work50%, report40%, presentation10%. Research Design accompanies it and requires four on-campus working groups with pass/fail participation; remote or substitute assessment is unavailable. Diagnostic English testing and required refresher are mandatory without extra EC. BSA ordinarily requires42EC first-year credits, subject to exceptions. Individual open choices require prior board approval, at least12EC level300 and at most6EC level100. Foreign choices may additionally include at most one6EC master course, not reusable later. Eligible university/listed minors are exempt from prior approval, but AI students may not enrol in the university Data Science or Basics of AI minors. Course-manual attendance and thesis/placement regulations apply. The general route claims no specialisation credential.
